what_happened: Dispatch description mis-locates an input: it states the six-mechanism survival analysis lives in specs/evidence/seam-gluing-ray-product/one-sided-count-move-refutation.lean, but that file contains no mechanism table and the word 'six' does not appear in it. The table is the 'Mechanism-by-mechanism measurement' section of the originating probe's archived research report in the source repository. Resolved at plan time as a citation decision (cite the durable probe paths, not the renumberable archived task directory) rather than a research gap.

Caught at plan authoring time that generate-context-line-counts.sh refuses to run from the agent-system source store (explicit diagnostic, nonzero exit) and must be invoked as the DEPLOYED copy .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh even though it rewrites the source index-entries.json files. A nearby precedent plan names the source-store path, which would have failed mid-phase; every invocation in this plan names the deployed entry point.

Ran suite_selection_select once as a single multi-path call over each phase's whole Files-to-modify set before writing its Tier Justification, then confirmed with validate-artifact.sh; the validator's under-verification warning named the deployed-corpus suites the source-store run omitted (test-lean-src-roots.sh, test-sapience-capture.sh), and the plan now validates with zero warnings.

Plan's Risk table characterized the sibling note's probe-citation overlap with the originating report's mechanism table as 'three' files; direct comparison during Phase 1 grounding found four overlapping files (ladder-cell-refutation.lean, ladder-cell-index-obstructions.lean, ladder-residue-index-refutation.lean, ladder-joint-index-refutation.lean). Governing conclusion unaffected: the two six-file sets still do not coincide, and the note never transcribes either set's count.

Phase 3's verify-touched.sh selected 23 suites for the 4 touched paths; 22 passed and test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh failed via its own internal 600s per-suite TIMEOUT. run-all.sh classified it (EXPECTED) with '1 expected, 0 NEW' -- it is a pre-registered known-failure (.claude/scripts/tests/known-failures.txt: load-sensitive, attributed to harness-level per-suite-timeout-vs-load interaction, explicitly confirmed unrelated to lint/content changes). Re-ran it standalone twice (bounded, ~580s and ~620s with an outer timeout wrapper) to rule out contention from the concurrent 23-suite run; it still timed out in isolation, consistent with the known-failures.txt classification rather than anything caused by this task's markdown/JSON-only edits. The OWED fallback's separate 98-suite run (triggered because ladder-counter-observables.md has no suite mapping) passed 98/98 clean. Treating verify-touched.sh's overall exit 1 as discharged on the strength of 0 NEW failures, per run-all.sh's own EXPECTED/NEW distinction.

Phase 4's verify-touched.sh over the task's five touched paths reproduced the same test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh timeout seen in Phase 3 (22/23 selected suites passed, 1 EXPECTED/0 NEW), plus a separate 98-suite OWED-fallback run (triggered by the two unmapped markdown paths) passing 98/98 clean. Overall exit 1 attributable solely to the pre-registered known-failure documented in known-failures.txt; discharged on 0 NEW failures, consistent with Phase 3's disposition.

Plan-time grounding (declaration resolution, baseline capture, probe-file verification) in Phase 1 meant Phase 2's note authoring and Phase 3's registration/cross-linking proceeded with zero rework: every backticked identifier in the finished note resolved on the first check, the note landed at 84 lines on the first draft (within the 70-110 target band), and generate-context-line-counts.sh --write touched exactly the three expected entries with no unexpected drift.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped '.claude-extensions.json' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
